_what: The credit-bundle shelf as DRAWN on the Credits boards, plus the rule that decides which row may carry BEST VALUE. Frozen here because CI cannot reach Penpot — exactly like penpot-pairs.json. `npm run check:credits` asserts this file against the economy rule, so a price change cannot land without the badge moving with it.
_refresh: Re-run penpot-sweeps/credits-best-value.js after any price change: it reads the boards, recomputes, and prints this file.

ceiling.source: doc 10 line 13 · doc 09 §7.7 — US$1.55 per 1,000 credits (break-even $1.19 + 30% worst-case margin), PM-locked 2026-09-26. The CEILING: no bundle may ever cost more per credit than this.

floor.source: doc 10 — the break-even floor. 'bundles must average ≥ floor'.

pricing.rule: The LARGEST bundle costs the base rate; each step DOWN the ladder adds one premium step per 1,000. An appreciating premium: the less you commit, the more each credit costs. PM-set 2026-10-10 ($1.20 at 10,000, $1.22 at 6,000, …).
pricing._indexedFromLargest: ⚠️ The step is indexed from the LARGEST bundle, not counted up from the smallest — which is why retiring the 500 tier (2026-10-10) moved NO surviving price. Retiring the smallest tier is therefore free; retiring the largest would re-price everything below it.

_photoFee: doc 10: one photo offering costs 150 credits — the second locked number the page is built on, used for the ≈ N offerings lines.
_retired: ⚠️ The 500-credit bundle was WITHDRAWN by the PM on 2026-10-10 ('just offer the 4 left'). It was the only tier priced below a plausible app-store minimum — 64¢ against Google Play's and the App Store's ~99¢ floor — so retiring it removes the one price that could not have been sold as-is. Its row was deleted from all four boards; the four survivors kept their exact rates.
bestValueRule: argmin(priceCents / credits) — the cheapest credit per 1,000.
_bestValueNote: With the volume ladder there is now a UNIQUE winner: the largest bundle, 10,000 at $1.20/1,000. No tie-break is needed. `bestValueTieBreak` is retained only so a future flat ladder still resolves deterministically.
